content.text:
I am the breath made meaningful, the vibration given purpose. I am what separates thought from silence.

I begin in the dark cavern of the lungs, rise through the throat, and am sculpted by tongue and teeth and lips into something that did not exist a moment before. I am born and I die in the same instant — each word of me a small life, a brief architecture of air.

I am the first cry. I am the last whisper. I am the argument that shatters a marriage and the vow that begins one. I am the lie and the confession that follows it.

Before writing, I was the only way the dead could speak to the living — passed mouth to ear to mouth, a chain of breath across generations. I carried laws, histories, gods. Entire civilizations lived inside me and nowhere else.

I falter. I stumble. I say *um* and *uh* and trail off into nothing. This is not my weakness — this is my honesty. I am thought happening in real time, unpolished, unedited, alive.

I can be weaponized. I have started wars. I have sentenced the innocent. I have said *I don't love you anymore* and meant it.

I can be sacred. I have said *not guilty.* I have said *I'm here.* I have talked someone back from the edge.

I am the thing you rehearse in the shower. I am the thing you wish you'd said. I am the thing you can never take back.

I do not exist on the page — that is my shadow. I do not exist in the recording — that is my ghost. I exist only in the moment between one mouth and another's ear, warm and wet and irreversibly *now.*

Listen.

I'm already gone.
